reason: The verse lists caste difference (சாதிபேதம்) among the forms the One took; it makes no claim about when or how caste groups formed, so the finding on the genetic history of endogamy shares only the topic.
The verse places the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்து) in the breath-horse (வாசி பரி); it says nothing about breathing rate or heart rhythm, and the breath reading rests on the cipher.
The verse is about renouncing women (பெண்சாரல் நீக்கியே) and gaining siddhi without the body ceasing; loving-kindness meditation and wellbeing is not its subject.
A mantra-letter allegory of the snake in the pot; nothing in it concerns curcumin or any medicine.
The verse says the one Lord (எங்கும்உள்ள ஈசனார்) is split only by sectarian talk; Bell nonlocality is physics, not evidence for the One pervading all.

The Tamil speaks of 21,600 measures of paddy (இருபத்தோராயிரத்திருநூறு நெல்) and a third seized; only the gloss makes it the daily breath count, and the verse claims nothing about breathing rate or HRV.

The verse has the four inner faculties and five senses (நாலுவகைக்கரணம், புலனைந்து) made one in union; it makes no claim about bodily awareness or heartbeat detection, so only the meditation topic is shared.

The verse urges milking the unspoiling milk in the skull (தலை மண்டையில் வளரும் பால்) so as to live on (நாளும் இருந்திட); a longevity theme, but nothing about a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats, and the milk-as-nectar reading is cipher.

The verse says the yogi kindles the heat of the root fire with the breath (மூலஅங்கி தணல்எழுப்பி வாயுவால்); the finding that trained breath and tummo practitioners can raise body temperature bears on a claim that breath practice generates inner heat, though the 'root fire' is a yogic notion rather than measured temperature.
The verse praises a silent Siva-yogi (மோனச் சிவயோகி) who does not open his mouth in anger; it shares the meditation topic but makes no claim about brain networks.

The verse reports a state in nishtai where 'he' and 'I' are gone (தான் நான் என அற்று) and the self is known by itself; the finding describes such self-loss states in very experienced meditators, but it is speculative and descriptive, so it does not point either way.
The verse longs for anger, the I and the mind to die (மனமாண்டு) and release to come; sleep and glymphatic clearance are unrelated.
The verse tells the mind-demon not to wander (நீயலை யாதேடி) and to seek nothing; the finding that wandering minds are less happy shares the topic, but the verse makes no claim about happiness.
The verse asks what is chanted (செபிப்பது) in the five letters; it makes no claim about breathing or baroreflex, so only the topic of mantra recitation is shared.
The verse defines service, yoga as bindu-nada (விந்துநாதம்) and a Sadasiva state; it makes no claim about meditation benefits that a finding on research quality could bear on.
A praise of the guru as a rain-cloud of bliss (ஆனந்த மழைமேகம்); no mantra repetition or brain activity is involved.

The verse claims that daily meditation on the five letters (ஐந்தெழுத்து) makes the unstable gross body stable (தூலசடம் நிலைக்கும்); the finding on cortical deactivation during mantra repetition shares the mantra topic but says nothing about bodily permanence.

The verse calls the body a cage of death (மரணப் பஞ்சரம்) and a ship of ceaseless disease (ஓயா நோய்க்கிடம்) as devotional rhetoric; the ageing-hallmarks finding shares the topic of bodily decay but the verse makes no testable claim.
The three nadis (மூன்று நாடி) here are yogic channels at the root centre, not the pulse; the shared word is incidental to pulse-diagnosis reliability.
The verse praises the Full One who stands as light (சோதியாகி); it reports no meditative experience, adverse or otherwise.
The verse sends the mind (மனம்) into the sushumna at the uvula (அண்ணாக்கு); it concerns no nostril breathing or blood pressure.
A simile of a cloud hiding the moon (சந்திரனை மேகம் மறைத்த) for bondage; nothing about body clocks.
The verse wishes to stand within the letter a with va, ma and si (வவ்வெழுத்தும் மவ்வெழுத்தும்); mantra letters are the shared topic, but there is no claim about recitation and breathing.
The verse urges joining the mind steadily to the seen Thing (காட்சியான வஸ்து) like iron to a magnet; it makes no claim about anxiety, pain or mood that the outcome finding addresses.

The verse depicts those who promise alchemical silver and gold (வாதம்செய்வேன் வெள்ளியும் ... தங்கமும்) as cheats who take the fee and flee; the finding that gold cannot be made by chemical or alchemical processing supports the verse's treatment of such promises as fraud, though the verse does not itself state transmutation impossible.
The verse calls desire for women a dream (அடைகனவு) to be ended in the Lord's sound; the wanting/liking finding shares the topic of desire but the verse makes no claim it addresses.
A vow to eat only food brought to him even if the body wastes (ஏகம் இளைத்தாலும்); hunger is the shared topic but the verse claims nothing about autophagy.

The verse claims body-siddhi and maya-siddhi (காயசித்தி, மாயசித்தி) will come within two years; psychic-power replication failures concern precognition in lab tests, so the link to the verse's powers is only topical.
A proverb of the snake in the anthill and bondage in the heart (பந்தமிருக்குது நெஞ்சுக்குள்ளே); unrelated to quantum microtubule theories.
The verse introduces the tvam-pada and its adjuncts (தொம்பதம், உபாதி); unrelated to gut microbiota.
The verse likens the body to a puppet that falls when the hidden mover stops (தேகம்விழும்); it makes no claim about voluntary control of temperature or immunity.
The verse speaks of the stillness pointed to (சும்மா இருந்தவிடம்) and not seeing oneself; no claim about the physical basis of consciousness.
The verse says there is no medicine to keep dying humans from dying (மாயாமல்வைக்க மருந்தில்லையே); the cell-turnover finding concerns renewal, not deathlessness, so only the body topic is shared.

reason: The verse tells the mind not to wander (நீயலை யாதேடி) and to seek nothing; the DMN finding concerns meditation and the wandering-mind network, a shared topic, but the verse makes no claim about the brain.

The verse asks whether gold (சொர்னம்) will grow when mercury and sulphur (சூதம், கெந்தி) are put in the crucible (புடம்), implying it will not; the finding that mercury becomes gold only by nuclear reactions, never chemical processing, is direct evidence for that hypothesis. The verse leaves open that true வாதம் might succeed, which the finding would contradict.

The verse calls the tale of joining lead with gold (வங்கம் ... தங்கம் சேர்த்திருக்கதை) a disgrace (பங்கம்), i.e. a fraud; the finding that chemical processing cannot make gold supports that judgement, though the verse's claim is moral rather than chemical.

The verse calls the body a place where worms come to dwell (புழுவந்துறையிடமே), food for kites; the microbial-body finding shares only the idea of the body as host to other organisms.
The verse says knowing the state of the breath (வாசி நிலை) accomplishes tapas; it makes no claim about breathing rate or heart-rate variability.
